why: The answer gives the correct truth-table rules for && and ||, but it only states the rules and does not apply them to values or relate them to any other part of the code.

concepts.quote: p && q is true only when both are true; p || q is false only when both are false.
concepts.why: This is the correct definition of && and ||, stated as a rule.
The answer says nothing about the order in which operands are evaluated or about skipping the right operand.
The answer makes no separate claim about the boolean type itself.
